name: Headway vs Thriveworks
title: Headway vs Thriveworks: Credentialing Platform vs W2 Employment
description: Compare Headway (free credentialing for independent therapists) vs Thriveworks (W2 employment with benefits). Understand private practice vs employment models.

summary.bottom_line: Headway and Thriveworks represent fundamentally different career models. Headway is a free credentialing platform helping therapists build independent private practices. Thriveworks is an employer offering W2 jobs ($75K-$150K salary) with benefits, no-show protection, and 340+ locations. Choose based on whether you want independence or employment stability.

key_differences.relationship: Headway: 1099 Independent | Thriveworks: W2 Employee or 1099
key_differences.income_model: Headway: Per-session earnings | Thriveworks: Salary + benefits
key_differences.risk: Headway: Business owner risk | Thriveworks: Employee stability
key_differences.autonomy: Headway: Full control | Thriveworks: Company structure

sections.heading: Two Paths for Therapists
sections.content: Headway and Thriveworks offer fundamentally different career paths. Headway enables private practice by handling insurance credentialing and billing for free - you're an independent business owner. Thriveworks is a clinician-founded company with 340+ locations offering W2 employment with salary ($75K-$150K), health insurance, no-show protection, and paid liability insurance. The choice is entrepreneurship vs employment.

sections.heading: Economics Compared
sections.content: With Headway, you earn per session based on insurance reimbursements minus Headway's share. Your income scales with volume and you keep the upside. With Thriveworks, you earn a predictable salary ($75K-$150K depending on role and location) plus benefits valued at thousands more annually. Thriveworks' no-show protection means you're paid even when insured clients cancel - a significant advantage over private practice.

sections.heading: Lifestyle Considerations
sections.content: Headway offers maximum flexibility - set your own hours, see clients you choose, work from anywhere. But you handle your own health insurance, liability coverage, retirement, and marketing. Thriveworks handles all of that but within a company structure. Note that Thriveworks PTO is limited (8 hrs/month accrual, 80 hr cap) and Glassdoor reviews mention compensation concerns (2.1/5 stars for pay).

recommendations.when: You want maximum independence, higher earning potential, and control over your practice.
You value stability, benefits, no-show protection, and not having to run a business.
You're experienced and have referral sources or marketing skills.
You're early-career and want support building experience with guaranteed income.

faqs.a: Thriveworks pays clinicians when private insured and self-pay clients no-show or late cancel. This is a significant advantage over private practice where no-shows directly impact income.

faqs.q: Can I earn more with Headway than Thriveworks?
faqs.a: Potentially yes. High-volume private practitioners using Headway can out-earn Thriveworks salaries, but you also bear more risk, pay for your own benefits, and handle business operations.

faqs.q: What are the downsides of Thriveworks?
faqs.a: Glassdoor reviews cite limited PTO (8 hrs/month), compensation concerns (2.1/5 star rating for pay), and less autonomy than private practice. Research thoroughly before accepting.
